summary.headline: Gopal Snacks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.9% YoY to INR 461.5 crore and EBITDA margin reached 9.0%, with FY27 guidance of INR 1,800-1,900 crore and 8.9% EBITDA margin maintained.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 22.9% YoY to INR 461.5 crore (up 9.3% QoQ), and H1 revenue rose 26.7% to INR 883.9 crore. EBITDA rose 72% YoY to INR 41.6 crore, with margin at 9.0% versus 6.4% a year earlier and 7.4% in Q1. Reported PAT of INR 45.9 crore includes a net exceptional gain of INR 35.3 crore, so underlying profit before exceptional items was INR 25.9 crore. Management said Gujarat run-rate is below its INR 100 crore/month aspiration, and that the full INR 36.4 crore fire insurance claim was received in October 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +72% YoY, +32% QoQ; margin vs 6.4% in Q2 FY26 and 7.4% in Q1 FY27
Includes net exceptional gain of INR 35.3 crore
vs INR 28.2 crore in H1 FY26; includes INR 35.3 crore net exceptional gain (INR 21.8 crore in H1 FY26)

segments.name: Namkeen
segments.commentary: H1 value growth 18.3% but volume growth only 8.6%; Q2 volume up 8% QoQ and 15% YoY. Grammage cuts are being taken SKU by SKU because the company is not market leader in several namkeen products.

segments.name: Gathiya
segments.commentary: Q2 sales up 25.6% YoY. Management said the company is taking share, as the category typically grows 15-18%.

segments.name: Wafers
segments.commentary: Q2 sales up 40% YoY; wafers grew 59% in focus states. Management plans about 30 wafer distributors added within 50-70 days, with Cristos positioned as upmarket and Gopal Wafers receiving trade margins.

segments.name: Snack Pellets and extruded snacks
segments.commentary: Q2 sales up 23% YoY; snack pellets grew 43% in focus states.

segments.name: Focus states
segments.commentary: Focus-state revenue about INR 132 crore in the quarter, growing about 35%. Maharashtra run-rate about INR 66 crore per quarter (INR 22 crore per month) and UP about INR 19 crore in the current quarter.

segments.name: Gujarat
segments.commentary: Core state revenue flat QoQ and below the INR 100 crore/month aspiration. Distributor count held near 311-312 for several quarters by design to protect distributor economics.

segments.name: Non-palm-oil products (bakery, cupcakes, suji, rusk, noodles)
segments.commentary: Contributed 3.25% of current top line; target 4.5% by FY27 end and 6.5% next year.

segments.name: New channels (railways, modern trade, quick commerce, exports)
segments.commentary: H1 railways INR 3.77 crore (vs INR 2.34 crore), modern trade INR 3.63 crore (vs INR 2.1 crore), quick commerce INR 7.07 crore (vs INR 3.48 crore). Exports near INR 1 crore in October vs INR 50-60 lakh average before. FY27 target INR 30-35 crore; FY28 target INR 75-90 crore.

segments.name: Joint ventures
segments.commentary: Manendragarh JV at INR 3.5-4 crore per month and at capacity; Kashipur about INR 1.25 crore per month; Hiriyur about INR 85 lakh per month.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR 1,800-1,900 crore, with EBITDA margin of 8.9%; H1 already in that range and H2 expected similar.
Management aspires to double-digit EBITDA margin, contingent on easing raw material inflation ('once the war scenario eases out').
Growth of at least 20% a year is targeted; about 6-7% of growth expected from network expansion and the rest from organic growth and new products.
Current momentum is 22-23% growth, per management.
Dual-servicing outlets to reach 65-70% by FY27 end (42% at September end, 43.5% at October end).
Distributor additions of about 220 expected in calendar 2026, against an earlier 250 target ('not exactly on track').
A&P spend expected at around 1% of revenue for the full year, similar to H1.
H2 operating cash flow expected to be better than H1, aided by insurance proceeds and inventory reduction from about INR 200 crore to INR 100-120 crore.
Besan unit at Nagpur (commenced September) expected to save about INR 3 crore a year in transport costs.
Laminate key-line-dimension changes worth about INR 6.7 crore annualised; benefit expected mainly next year due to two-month laminate stock.
capex_capacity: Besan manufacturing unit commissioned in September 2026 at Nagpur, reducing transport from Rajkot.
Company-level capacity utilisation about 37-38%; management said grammage cuts also depressed utilisation.
Operating leverage contributed about 1% of margin benefit in H1 FY27.
Manendragarh JV has run out of capacity; Kashipur and Hiriyur JVs are below that level.
Chana storage up to about 50% higher than last year, with chana stock expected to last until mid-January and potato until mid-December.
demand_pricing: Cumulative inflation impact to H1 is about 5.5% versus FY26 average: about 4% passed through grammage, 0.6% through price, and 0.7-0.8% through trade discount and mix.
Sequential Q1 to Q2 inflation impact on gross margin was 2.3%: 1.1% from grammage, 0.4% from price, and 0.4% from trade discount and mix.
Raw material basket: palm oil about 27%, laminate/packaging about 22-23%, chana about 19%.
INR 10-plus price point contribution rose to about 21%; management expects about 3.5% of that category next quarter.
Management said the company will not chase volume at the cost of margins, and rivals are expected to need price hikes or grammage cuts.
Two local brands (Star, Kolhapur; Miraj, Nathdwara) shut down last quarter; no closures noted in Q2 so far.
Gokul, a brand run by a promoter relative's splinter group, is now treated as a regular competitor.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company satisfied with core-state (Gujarat) growth against the INR 100 crore/month run-rate aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not satisfied with the Gujarat run-rate and is aiming at INR 100 crore per month without cutting margins; pricing and grammage are being managed carefully.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin is from pricing versus mix and grammage?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin gain came from a mix of grammage correction, price correction, and about 0.4% from lower trade discount and mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume outlook in namkeen after price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 namkeen value grew 18.3% against 8.6% volume growth. Grammage cuts are taken SKU by SKU, and two new namkeen products are planned for next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What progress has been made on dual servicing of outlets?
qa_highlights.answer: Dual servicing reached 42% at September end and 43.5% at October end in Gujarat. The target is 65-70% by FY27 end, and 25-30 Western snacks ready-stock distributors will be added in Gujarat.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company growing 20% a year after FY27 and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will be at least 20% a year. H1 network additions of about 130 distributors contributed INR 13 crore, rising to about INR 60 crore in the full year and about INR 80 crore next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins reach double digits by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 8-9% guidance stands and double digit is an aspiration that depends on raw material inflation easing.

qa_highlights.question: What are the H2 CFO drivers, and why was H1 CFO weaker?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 CFO should be better because of the INR 36.4-36.5 crore insurance receipt and inventory falling from about INR 200 crore to INR 100-120 crore. H1 was weaker because of higher inventory, including about 50% more chana storage and laminate stock.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company handle competitors burning cash in Gujarat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competitors cannot sustain losses for long and will need to take price or grammage decisions; distributor count was held flat deliberately to protect per-distributor revenue.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: palm oil (about 27% of basket), laminate/packaging (about 22-23%) and chana (about 19%); management ties margin recovery to easing of the 'war scenario', so the 8-9% EBITDA guidance and the double-digit aspiration depend on input costs.
Gujarat core-state run-rate remains below the INR 100 crore/month aspiration; distributor count held near 311-312 by design, and competitors' cash burn is a stated concern.
Namkeen volume growth (8.6% in H1) lags value growth (18.3%) as grammage cuts are taken SKU by SKU; watch whether two planned new namkeen products arrive next quarter.
Network expansion is behind plan: about 220 distributor additions expected in calendar 2026 versus an earlier 250 target ('not exactly on track'); Nagpur/Maharashtra additions slower than expected.

Cash flow: H1 CFO weaker than usual due to higher inventory (laminate, chana storage up about 50%); H2 relies on insurance receipt of INR 36.4 crore and inventory falling from about INR 200 crore to INR 100-120 crore.
Drought and possible chana and potato price increases in the next financial year; management said pass-through will rely on mix, lower trade marketing and price/grammage moves.
Non-core channels (exports, railways, modern trade, quick commerce) targeted at INR 30-35 crore in FY27 and INR 75-90 crore in FY28; watch execution, with exports only about INR 1 crore in October.
key_quotes: So definitely we are not satisfied with this run rate in Gujarat.
So once the war scenario eases out, definitely we'll reach to double-digit margins.
So we have almost got 1% of the benefit as far as operating leverage is concerned, and that will continue to give us the benefit go ing forward also
Not exactly on track, but we are confident that in the full calendar year we will be able to add roughly 220 distributors.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on volume momentum (22-23% current growth, Gathiya and wafers ahead of category) and on operating leverage, but cautious on margins, saying double-digit EBITDA depends on easing raw material inflation. It was candid on shortfalls: Gujarat run-rate below aspiration, distributor additions not exactly on track, and H1 cash flow weaker.

adds.what: Besan manufacturing unit at Nagpur (commissioned September 2026), reducing transport from Rajkot

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 1,800-1,900 crore (roughly 21.5% midpoint growth on FY26 base implied; H1 already at INR 883.9 crore, +26.7%) was held with an 8.9% EBITDA margin, backed by share gains in gathiya/wafers, focus-state growth of about 35%, new channels targeting INR 30-35 crore, and a Nagpur besan unit, but no new plant capacity is being added and utilisation is only 37-38%.
